record.category: Telegram mirror/leech bot: remote-URL fetcher with operator-side storage

free_tier.stated: Published limits post: "Mirror: upto 80 GB/link; Leech: upto 80 GB/link (4gb support); Yt-dlp: upto 80 GB/link; Mega.nz Link: upto 80 GB/link; Daily Limit: Unlimited".
free_tier.notes: Unlimited refers to the daily count of links, not to bytes in flight; each link is capped at 80 GB.

per_object_cap.stated: 80 GB per link on every mode: mirror, leech, yt-dlp and MEGA.
per_object_cap.notes: 80 x 1024^3. The '(4gb support)' note next to leech is the vendor's own remark that Telegram's own file ceiling applies to a leeched file.

retention.stated: Not stated. A mirror lands in operator storage and a leech lands in the user's Telegram; no expiry is published for either.

egress.terms: The bot pulls from a remote URL and re-serves it: a mirror returns a link on the operator's host, a leech returns the file into the chat. No bandwidth figure or price is published.

record.interface_detail: A Telegram bot, not an HTTP service: the control channel is Telegram chat with @publicmirrorbot, and there is no documented REST endpoint. The bot's preview names a fallback bot and a support group rather than an API.
record.tooling: Telegram client only. Automating it means driving a Telegram user session, which is a real constraint for a client that wants a script rather than a chat window.
record.chaining: A resolver for links a normal client cannot fetch: a MEGA or yt-dlp URL goes in, a direct file comes out, and it bypasses the per-host limits a downloader would otherwise meet. It is the human-shaped version of what a debrid subscription does, with an 80 GB per-link ceiling instead of a monthly one.

limits.value: 80 GB per link (mirror, leech, yt-dlp, MEGA)
daily limit stated as unlimited; concurrent-task and queue limits are not published

record.limits_note: The 80 GB figure is generous for a free bot and is the only hard number the operator publishes. Nothing is said about how many tasks may run at once, which is where a shared public bot actually queues.
record.binding_note: At 1 TiB a month the link ceiling is what stops a single transfer: 80 GB is about 12 links to the monthly target, so a 1 TiB archive has to be split. The daily count is explicitly unlimited, so it cannot bind.

identity_cost.detail: A Telegram account is the only gate: any phone number that can receive the signup code. No email, payment or identity document is asked for by the bot.

record.reliability_note: A shared public bot with no SLA, with limits published in a channel post rather than on a stable web page. The channel listing includes a beta fallback bot.
record.confidence_note: The limits are the vendor's own post in the bot's linked updates channel, not a vendor specification page, and nothing was transferred. Moving to documented needs the numbers on a stable page; moving to measured needs one 80 GB job run and read.

evidence.proved: the limits post verbatim: 80 GB per link on mirror, leech, yt-dlp and MEGA, and 'Daily Limit: Unlimited'
the bot exists as 'Mirror Leech Bot 3' and links @PublicMirrorLeechGroup and @PublicMirrorLeechUpdates as its group and channel
3,088 members and 380 online, which is the scale signal for a public bot's queue
the same post states the daily limit as unlimited
the group has 3,143 members and 499 online
the bot page is live as 'Mirror Leech Bot 3'
the operator's limits post gives 80 GB per link on mirror

record.notes: Classified as a service because it resolves and fetches remote URLs rather than mirroring an account: a user hands it a URL and gets bytes back. The account-mirror bots in the same ledger were not recorded, because they only drive somebody's own cloud account.
